analysis:
The PR is CI-only. It changes .github/workflows/ci.yml, docs (build.md, test.md), a changelog entry, and offline CI test scripts. It touches no provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), key custody (A-003), prefix cache (T-041), fan helper (TB-010) or add-on hold socket (TB-012/TB-013). Those boundaries are unaffected.

The security-relevant change is that same-repo PR and push code (recursive checkout, Swift builds, test scripts) in the macOS test jobs can now run on Darkbloom Sandbox macOS runners when the plane grants a lane. Previously these jobs were pinned to literal Blacksmith runners. Visible controls in ci.yml head: workflow permissions are contents: read, the route job has `permissions: {}`, persist-credentials is false, cache saves are gated by SAVE_CACHES (master/dev pushes only), actions are SHA-pinned, and the fallback is Blacksmith. The updated tests (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py) still assert that routed jobs have read-only permissions with no id-token, secrets, environment, service or container, a timeout of at most 60 minutes, and that release and credentialed workflows keep literal runners. Fork PRs never contact the plane. Only exact label arrays are accepted. The `needs: [changes, route]` dependency is added and tested.

Unverified contracts, outside the supplied evidence:
- darkbloom-route.yml was not supplied.
- The sandbox VM isolation and ephemerality are unknown.
- The unseen cache save behavior on push runs routed to a sandbox lane is a possible cache-poisoning path into later restores, but the cache keys and restore scopes were not visible.
- Whether the fromJSON lookup resolves safely when a lane is missing from the routes map is unknown.
- scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py was only partly visible.

No concrete regression was established. I recommend a follow-up on route-workflow trust and cache-write scope.
